question: Should `socket.drain` remain an advisory event subject to normal slow-client shedding, or should OpenClaw introduce a bounded recoverable delivery contract for clients that use it for session cleanup?
rationale: The correct behavior under a stalled subscriber determines queueing, disconnect, replay, and client-recovery semantics; that is a public gateway-protocol choice rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Keep advisory delivery
options.body: Preserve the normal slow-client drop policy for `socket.drain`, document that clients reconcile through supported session state, and keep the new routing narrowly scoped.

options.title: Design recoverable delivery
options.body: Specify bounded buffering plus acknowledgement, replay, or explicit resynchronization before allowing clients to depend on drains for deterministic cleanup.

options.title: Pause the event addition
options.body: Defer the new event until its overload and recovery semantics have an approved gateway protocol design.

recommendation.title: Keep advisory delivery
recommendation.body: Preserve the normal slow-client drop policy for `socket.drain`, document that clients reconcile through supported session state, and keep the new routing narrowly scoped.
